column1: # Invented names written blind, by someone who had not seen the rules,
# to measure them: the name, the part of the profile's link after /in/
# or nothing, the first name a careful person greets them by, and ? for
# the family name, which this set does not ask. Lines starting with
# "# miss" are names read wrong today, see docs/names.md.
# Double first names and middle names
# Judgement: "Anna Lena" without hyphen is a fixed double name used together.
# Academic and professional titles before the name, German
Dr. h. c. mult. Waltraud Pesch
Dr. med. Dr. med. dent. Philipp Arens, MSc
Rechtsanwalt und Fachanwalt für Arbeitsrecht Sebastian Quast
# Only a title and a family name, or only initials
# The handle tells what the name does not
# Degrees, certifications and credentials after the name
Kathrin Vogel, PMP, CSM, SAFe® SPC
# Nicknames in quotes or brackets: the name they want to be called
# A quoted tagline is not a nickname.
Anke Rösler | Partnerin bei Rösler & Brandt
Ich helfe Selbstständigen, sichtbar zu werden | Franziska Sommer
Mareike Holt 🚀 Ich bringe dein Business auf Kurs
Dr. Kai Rehberg 👨‍⚕️ Hausarzt in Essen
# Unicode bold, italic, script and other styled letters
# Invisible and odd whitespace, decomposed letters
# Family name first, with and without comma
# Role or business words before or around the name
# Two people on one profile: no single first name to greet.
# Judgement: Seyed is an inherited honorific, the person is greeted by Ali.
# Judgement: Maria Grazia is one given name used together.
